thinking-strategies.alt: A problem branches into two strategies. Left: an algorithm, a step-by-step procedure that is slow and effortful but guarantees a solution if followed, for example trying every four-digit code from 0000 to 9999 on a lock. Right: a heuristic, a mental shortcut that is fast and easy and usually works but can mislead, for example trying the owner's birthday as the code first. A note under the heuristic defines the representativeness heuristic (judging by how well something matches a prototype) and the availability heuristic (judging by how easily examples come to mind). A note under the algorithm says both can be blocked by mental set (sticking with a method that worked before) and functional fixedness (seeing an object only in its usual use).
